title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. $\hat\pi_{0,3}$ is the profinite fundamental group of $\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, a free profinite group on two generators. It carries an outer action of $\mathfrak S_3$, generated by the involution $\sigma_\infty$ (swapping 0 and 1) and the 3-cycle $\rho$. The loops $l_0, l_1$ generate inertia at the punctures, with $\varepsilon_0 = \sigma_\infty\rho$ and $\varepsilon_0^2 = l_0$, and $L_0$ is the inertia subgroup at 0. $\mathcal M_{0,3}^{!\sim}$ is the group of automorphisms of the extension $\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}$ ($\hat\pi_{0,3}$ extended by $\mathfrak S_3$) that commute externally with $\mathfrak S_3$; $\mathcal M_{0,3}^{!\sim}[0]$ is the normaliser of $L_0$ inside it.

Previous page. For $u$ in this group Grothendieck writes $u(\sigma_\infty) = \eta\sigma_\infty$ and $u(\rho) = \xi\rho$. Normalising $L_0$ means $u(\varepsilon_0) = \varepsilon_0^\mu$ with $\mu \in \hat{\mathbb Z}^*$; he puts $\mu = 1 + 2\nu$. He then derives:
- (133): $\eta\,\sigma_\infty(\eta) = 1$ and $\xi\,\rho(\xi)\,\rho^2(\xi) = 1$. These are the involution and order-3 relations of the images.
- (134): $\xi = \eta\, l_1^\nu$, the 'relation des lacets' (loop relation).

This page states the resulting theorem.
- Elements of $\mathcal N_{0,3}^{!\sim}[0]$ correspond bijectively to pairs $(\xi,\eta)$ in $\hat\pi_{0,3}$ satisfying (133) and (134). They must also satisfy a 'condition liminaire': the elements $\eta\sigma_\infty$ and $\xi\rho$, with relations (132), must again generate the profinite extension $\hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}$. This is what makes the endomorphism an automorphism.
- $\nu \in \hat{\mathbb Z}$ is uniquely determined, and invertibility forces $2\nu+1 \in \hat{\mathbb Z}^*$ (the '$\nu$-liminaire' condition). In the body he says the liminaire condition implies it and wonders whether the converse holds. A later marginal note asserts that $2\nu+1 \in \hat{\mathbb Z}^*$ already follows from (133) and (134) alone, citing a theorem on p. 409.
- Inner automorphisms by $\lambda = l_0^n \in L_0$ correspond to $\xi = \eta = l_0^n l_1^{-n}$, with $\nu = 0$. More generally $L_0$ acts by $(\xi,\eta) \mapsto (l_0^n\xi l_1^{-n},\ l_0^n\eta l_1^{-n})$.
- The quotient $\mathcal M[0]/L_0$, i.e. outer automorphisms normalising inertia at 0 modulo $L_0$, is the set of solution pairs modulo this action. The set of pairs carries the twisted (crossed-homomorphism) group law $(\xi',\eta')(\xi,\eta) = (u'(\xi)\xi',\ u'(\eta)\eta')$, continued on the next page.

In modern terms this is the presentation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group as solutions $(\lambda,f)$ of Drinfeld-type equations, with $\lambda = 2\nu+1$. The 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations correspond to Drinfeld's relations (I) and (II); the pentagon is absent at this stage (genus 0, 3 points only). The purpose is to describe the outer automorphisms of $\hat\pi_{0,3}$ compatible with $\mathfrak S_3$ (the 'Teichmüller tower' at level $(0,3)$), into which $\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q)$ embeds.
errors: In (135) the target should be $\mathcal M_{0,3}^{!\sim}[0]$; the transcription reads '(ω)', which is probably '[0]' badly read.

In (136) the transcription has $\sigma_2$; it should be $\sigma_\infty$. Since $\rho(l_0) = l_1$ and $\sigma_\infty(l_0) = l_1$ (up to the chosen conventions), both $\xi$ and $\eta$ equal $l_0^n l_1^{-n}$, consistent with (134) at $\nu = 0$.

The marginal claim that $2\nu+1 \in \hat{\mathbb Z}^*$ follows from (133)–(134) alone is not proved here (deferred to p. 409). In Drinfeld's GT, $\lambda \in \hat{\mathbb Z}^*$ is imposed as an axiom (the monoid $\underline{GT}$ allows general $\lambda$), so the claim needs checking.
The body text leaves open whether the $\nu$-liminaire condition implies the full liminaire (generation) condition.

ideas.what: Parametrisation of $\mathfrak S_3$-compatible outer automorphisms of $\hat F_2$ normalising inertia at 0, by pairs $(\xi,\eta)$ subject to a 2-cycle relation, a 3-cycle relation and a 'loop relation' $\xi = \eta l_1^\nu$
ideas.where_published: Programme sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without explicit equations; this manuscript is unpublished

ideas.what: 'Condition liminaire': the images must again generate the extension, distinguishing automorphisms from endomorphisms (group versus monoid)
Claim that invertibility of the multiplier $2\nu+1$ follows from the 2- and 3-cycle relations plus the loop relation
Quotient by inertia conjugation $(\xi,\eta) \mapsto (l_0^n\xi l_1^{-n},\ l_0^n\eta l_1^{-n})$ and twisted group law $\xi'' = u'(\xi)\xi'$
ideas.modern_name: Crossed-homomorphism description of the GT group law, $(\lambda,f)(\lambda',f') = (\lambda\lambda',\ f\cdot\text{(twisted product)})$

missed.claim: An explicit, self-contained derivation of the two basic GT relations (2-cycle and 3-cycle, linked by a 'relation des lacets' with multiplier $\mu = 2\nu+1$), stated as a theorem on automorphisms of $\hat\pi_{0,3}$ commuting with $\mathfrak S_3$ and normalising inertia. This independently anticipates Drinfeld's relations (I)–(II).
missed.quote: Les éléments u de N_{0,3}^{!~}[0] ... sont en corr. biunivoque ... avec les couples (ξ,η) ... satisfaisant les relations (133)(134)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's own concrete equations for $\widehat{GT}$ at level $(0,3)$, relevant to the history and attribution of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.

missed.claim: Whether $2\nu+1 \in \hat{\mathbb Z}^*$ is automatic from the relations, and whether it already implies the generation ('liminaire') condition. This amounts to asking whether the monoid of solutions equals its group of invertible elements.
missed.quote: cette condition 2ν+1∈Ẑ* est conséquence des relations (133), (134), cf plus bas th. p. 409
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Bears on the open-ish comparison between $\underline{GT}$ (monoid) and $\widehat{GT}$, i.e. when endomorphisms satisfying the GT relations are automatically automorphisms.

deep.surprise_reason: The page gives Grothendieck's explicit pre-Drinfeld equations for $\mathfrak S_3$-equivariant automorphisms of $\hat\pi_{0,3}$, essentially GT relations (I)–(II) with a loop relation. Specialists know he worked on this, but the explicit theorem and the claim about automatic invertibility of the multiplier are not in the published record.
transcription_corrections: In (135) and (137), '$\mathcal M_{0,3}^{!\sim}(\omega)$' is likely $\mathcal M_{0,3}^{!\sim}[0]$.
'Si l'inclusion évidente' is probably 'Si l'inclusion évidente' / 'Or l'inclusion évidente'.
'commutent à ext$^t$' should read 'commutent ext$^t$ à'.
'indépendamment uniquement déterminé' is likely 'évidemment uniquement déterminé'.
